Issued at 311 AM EDT Mon Sep 14 2026

Pattern / Forecast Synopsis: 

Quick jet stream flow across the northern CONUS into southern Canada 
throughout the forecast period... 500mb ridge axis amplifies 
overhead as a shortwave ejects into the northern Plains, bringing 
with it a deep surge of warm and moist return flow through Tuesday. 
Focus of this moisture focuses along a slow-moving frontal boundary 
first set to be over northern Michigan late tonight into Tuesday, 
providing potential for efficient to perhaps heavy rainfall across 
the region, pending convective ingredient cooperation. The wave is 
set to flatten out as it continues northeast toward James Bay and 
eventually northern Quebec by midweek. Result will be the front 
passing through, but largely stalling out just to the south as zonal 
flow results in a parallel flow setup along the frontal boundary. 
Aforementioned zonal flow will continue to feed subtle 500mb 
shortwaves through this frontal zone, which could result in a split 
bag of drier conditions north and better shower potential south 
across the CWA as we progress through the remainder of the week. 

Details: 

The picture is big over the next couple days regarding the evolution 
of this incoming system... surface high pressure quickly builds 
across the region today, with ample dry air to work with (blatantly 
visible on the 14/00Z APX sounding). This wedge of dry air will be 
vital to forecast evolution across the region over the next 36-48 
hours. Skies start quite clear today, but with the approach of the 
Plains shortwave, anticipating resultant return flow to commence 
warm and moist advection. Considering how dry it's going to be at 
the surface, will start to see moisture advection show aloft before 
it does at the surface, as high cloud builds through the afternoon 
into the evening. Speaking of that low level drier air... efficient 
mixing processes will allow for a dip in dewpoints through the 
afternoon, which could lead to a backdoor shot at some elevated fire 
parameters, but for the time being, stronger flow aloft should wait 
until later in the day / evening, which should stave off any fire 
concerns.

Deeper moisture does start to manifest tonight, with current 
guidance supporting best moisture pooling through the night favoring 
a corridor from northern Wisconsin through central and eastern 
upper, with lesser saturation favored the farther south one goes. 
Result will be more concentrated rainfall across eastern upper into 
the Tip of the Mitt through Tuesday morning. Current guidance 
suggests a general 0.50-1.00"+ across eastern upper, with spots in 
the Tip of the Mitt likely seeing totals that land a tenth or two on 
either side of 0.50". Rest of northern lower likely holds 0.25" or 
less (perhaps locally up to 0.50"). Firmly anticipating the rain 
shield to more or less be directly overhead by Tuesday, which should 
lead to a wet start to the day for most, if not, all of the region. 
Going through Tuesday, lift generally decreases through the region, 
which should lead to the erosion of the rain shield with time, and 
thus lessening shower coverage through the day as the front itself 
passes through. As such, could be quite the gap between better rains 
to the north and lesser rainfall to the south... and to add insult 
to injury for those looking for rain, the front looks to flare up 
again later Tuesday into Tuesday night, but current signals from 
guidance suggests that it will occur to the south of the region. 

Another factor to contend with this system will be a gradually 
tightening pressure gradient, drumming up stronger winds across the 
region Monday night through Tuesday. Echoing previous forecaster's 
thoughts, general warm advection regime should mute much of the low 
level jet's mixing abilities via an inversion just off the deck. 
Make no mistake, it will turn quite breezy, but for now, looks like 
most places see 25-35mph wind gusts at times Monday night through 
the day Tuesday, perhaps pushing 40mph along the immediate 
lakeshores. 

With the front clearing the region by Wednesday and the pressure 
gradient weakening considerably owing to another surface high moving 
overhead, much less breezy conditions to manifest, with post-frontal 
airmass in place as well. Front set to remain stalled downstate 
through the rest of the week, but will occasionally see waves pass 
through this frontal zone... some of which may hold just enough 
moisture extent to the north to drum up some shower chances 
Wednesday night - Thursday and again through the weekend, 
particularly the farther south one goes. Axis of heaviest rainfall 
from these waves should be suppressed well to the south of the 
region, thus limiting any additional appreciable rainfall potential 
across the region, and likely resulting in ample dry time.
